These two appeals are being disposed of by this common judgment since M.A.C.M.A.No.260 of 2020 filed by the injured, seeking enhancement of the compensation and M.A.C.M.A.No.28 of 2020 filed by the Insurance Company, are directed against the very same order and decree, dated 02.07.2019, passed in M.V.O.P.No.156 of 2016 on the file of the Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-I Additional District and Sessions Judge, Adilabad (for short "the Tribunal").
2.

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the learned Tribunal.

3. The brief facts of the case are that the petitioner filed a claim-petition under Section 166 (1) (a) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 read with Rule 455 of Andhra Pradesh Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989,
claiming compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in a road accident, which occurred on 23.06.2015.

It is stated that on 23.06.2015, while the petitioner, along with one Alwala Bapu Rao @ Babu Rao, was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.AP-1-A-9689 from Kagaznagar towards Asifabad for attending labour work and when they reached Kagaznagar Cross NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020 Road, the rider of motorcycle drove the same in a rash and negligent manner at high speed and lost control over the motorcycle, due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained (1) degloving injury to left foot; (2) crush injury to left hand; (3) comminuted fracture of left 3rd finger; (4) fracture of left Glenoid; (5) fracture of 1 to 4 left ribs and (6) head injury apart from other injuries all over the body.

It is further stated that immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital, Bellampalli and obtained first aid and from there she was shifted to Fortune Medicare Hospital, Karimnagar for better treatment, where she underwent surgical operation and implants were inserted over the fracture injuries.

During the course of treatment, the petitioner undergone several tests, examination and X-rays and she was discharged from the above hospital with an advice to take complete bed rest and follow up treatment and she spent Rs.4,50,000/- towards medical expenses.

4. Basing on a complaint, the Police, Rebbena, registered a case in Crime No.21 of 2015 against the rider of the Motorcycle, for the offence punishable under Section 338 of I.P.C.
5.
It is further stated that the petitioner was hale and healthy and aged about 45 years and was earning Rs.8,000/- per month by doing labour work.

Due to the aforesaid injuries sustained by her,
NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020 she was unable to sit and stand properly and unable to attend her daily activities easily.
Due to the injuries she suffered lot of pain both mentally and physically.

7. Respondent No.2-United India Insurance Company Limited, filed counter denying the averments made in the claim-petition and also specially denied the involvement of the offending vehicle, the manner in which the accident took place, injuries sustained by the petitioner, treatment undergone by her and the expenditure incurred by her.

It is specifically contended that the rider of the motorcycle was not having valid driving licence at the time of the accident, as such, the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation and prayed to dismiss the claim-petition.

8. Basing on the above pleadings, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the accident took place as alleged by the petitioner on 23.06.2015 while the petitioner along with respondent No.1 was proceeding on motorcycle bearing No.AP-1-A-9689 from Kagaznagar towards Asifabad to attend NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020 labour work and at about 9 a.m. when they reached at Kagaznagar X-road, all of sudden the respondent No.1/rider of motorcycle drove the motorcycle in rash and negligent manner with high speed and lost control over it and fell down on the ground due to which the petitioner sustained injuries, or whether there was any contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner?
2. Whether the petitioner sustained injuries? If so, whether it leads to disability as alleged?
3. Whether the motorcycle bearing No.AP-1-A-9689 was stood insured with respondent No.2/Insurance Company?

And if so, does the policy cover the risk of petitioner and if so, was there any breach of policy conditions by the owner/respondent No.2?
4.
Whether the petitioner is entitled to any compensation?

If so, what is the quantum and against whom?
5.
To what relief?

9. Having heard both sides, the learned Tribunal has recasted the issues and framed the following issues:-
1. Whether the accident dated 23.06.2015 was due to the rash and negligent driving of Motorcycle bearing No.AP-01- A-9689 and the said accident resulted in injuries to the petitioner?

10. Before the Tribunal, on behalf of the claimant, P.Ws.1 to 3 were examined and Exs.A1 to 14 were marked.
On behalf of the respondents, R.W.1 was examined and Exs.B1 and B2 were marked.

11. After considering the contents of the claim-petition, counter filed by the insurance company and evaluating the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the Tribunal held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the rider of the motorcycle and allowed the M.V.O.P in part and granted compensation of Rs.3,84,000/- together with costs and interest at 7.5%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization payable by the respondents jointly and severally.

12. Being aggrieved by the said quantum of compensation and liability, the petitioner filed M.A.C.M.A.No.260 of 2020 seeking enhancement of compensation on the following grounds:-
(i) that the learned Tribunal, without considering the income of the petitioner and the injuries sustained by her, had awarded meager amount of compensation.
NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020 (ii) that the learned Tribunal did not consider the evidence placed by the petitioner with regard to the disability sustained by her.
(iii) that the learned Tribunal awarded meager amounts under the heads of transportation, medical expenses, extra nourishment, incidental expenses, pain and sufferance and prayed to allow the appeal.

13. Aggrieved by the liability imposed on it, respondent No.2- insurance company also preferred M.A.C.M.A.No.28 of 2020 on the following grounds:-
(i) that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and the petitioner being the pillion rider is not covered under Ex.B1 and Ex.A6 i.e., insurance policy and inspite of there being no liability, the learned Tribunal had imposed liability on the insurance company ignoring the fact that Ex.B1 is an Act policy and the insurance company is not required to cover any risk of the pillion rider.
(ii) that the learned Tribunal ought to have restricted the award against respondent No.1-rider-cum-owner of the motorcycle and so also the learned Tribunal has taken the income of the injured at Rs.4,500/- without any basis and awarded NNR, J The United India Insurance Company ... vs Pentaparthi Kamala And Another on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80124210/

14. Respondent No.1-rider-cum-owner of the motorcycle did not choose to contest the appeals.

15. Having heard Mr.S.Surender Reddy, learned counsel for the appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No.260 of 2020 and Sri Srinivasa Rao Vutla, learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company i.e.,
appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No.28 of 2020 and perusal of the material on record, the following points that arose for consideration.
(1) Whether the petitioner has made out any valid ground to enhance the compensation?
(2) Whether the insurance company has made out any ground to interfere with the order passed by the learned Tribunal with regard to the liability imposed on it?

16.Point No.2 relates to liability of insurance company:-
NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020

The main grievance of the learned Standing Counsel for the insurance company, appellant in M.A.C.M.A.No.28 of 2020 is that Ex.B1-policy being an Act policy and not being the comprehensive package policy, the petitioner being the pillion rider is not covered under the said Act policy.
17.
Admittedly, the petitioner was pillion rider and it is self made accident committed by the rider of the motorcycle.

It is not disputed and it is clearly established by way of the evidence that the accident occurred only due to the rider of the motorcycle as he drove the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner at highspeed and lost control, thereby the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.
It is not the case of the petitioner with regard to the involvement of another vehicle in the present case.
In view of the accident being self made accident, the only issue which has to be considered in the present case is whether the liability can be imposed upon the insurance company.

18. Admittedly, as per Ex.B1-policy the said motorcycle was insured with respondent No.2 vide policy bearing No.0519823115P102388582 valid from 02.06.2015 to 01.06.2016 and the said policy was subsisting as on the date of accident which occurred on 23.06.2015.
On perusal of the said policy, premium of Rs.588/- is paid and it appears to be coverage of third party.
Since NNR, J Macmas_28 and 260_2020 the said policy is only in respect of third party, the question which arose whether the pillion rider can be treated as third party.

19. In view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Simla v.
Tilak Singh and others 1 wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that the pillion rider is not covered in the Act Policy and the Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the pillion rider.

P.W.2 conducted surgery on left foot "Extensive Degloving of Left Foot; dead skin tissue excised, K-wire fixation were done and proximal phalanx of left great toe and 4th and 5th after medical care left distal, radius fracture K-wire fixation were done.
